svg.title: Gesture dispatch pipeline
svg.desc: How one input event travels from a DOM listener on the canvas, through view routing and binding assembly, matching, ranking and eligibility, to an invoked action or unhandled.
svg.text: One input, from DOM event to action
useGestureDispatcher (the React seam, steps 1 to 2) feeds Dispatcher.handleInput (pure, steps 3 to 8).
1 A DOM event reaches the canvas
Pointer, wheel, pinch and context-menu listeners sit on the canvas
element; key and paste listeners on window.
A pointerdown or wheel first calls activate(), making this canvas the
A keydown is dropped unless isActive(): only the active scope acts on
A press dispatches at once with stage: 'press'. Its drag copy waits
until the pointer passes the drag threshold; a release before that
With views set, the resolver picks the view under the pointer, and a
pointerdown pins that pointer to its view until release. Keys and paste
go to the view the last pointer event landed in.
The view brings its own dispatcher, hit tests (affordanceAt,
classifyTarget), clientToWorld, dep overlay and rule context. Without
views, everything is the root view.
3 Is a gesture already open on this channel?
A pointermove, pointerup, pointercancel or held-key release belongs to
the handle open under its gesture id (pointer-<id>, key-held-<key>)
Everything else (press, drag start, key, wheel, click, pinch) goes on.
assembleScopedBindings tags each binding with a tier:
tools held by a hotkey: hotkey tier, newest hold first
tools marked always or claimed: ambient tier
every registered action's bindings: ambient, or hotkey when
Left out: tools whose capability tags the current mode forbids, and
bindings whose views do not include this view.
matchSorted keeps the bindings whose spec matches the event (kind,
key, modifiers, target, phase). An exclusive affordance claim first bars
bindings that do not consult the affordance. Survivors sort by tier,
preferViewScoped then moves bindings that name this view to the front.
Only when a rule context is supplied.
filterEligible drops candidates whose action's eligible rule is false
preferContextual: within a run tied on tier and specificity, an action
whose rule holds moves ahead of one with no rule.
Each action is tried once, even when several bindings point at it.
no registered action for the id: warn, try the next
build the action's deps from its requires
enabled(deps, point) returns anything but true: try the next
ongoing: start(ctx, opts). An empty handle means it declined: try
the next candidate. Otherwise the handle is held in flight under its
gesture id, then handled; later moves pump it through step 3.
no invoker: handled, as a deliberate no-op
yoke's active child to this scope.
isActive() asks whether this scope is
The scope's own tool, or its yoke's
